for_the_owner: Judgment call: TouchBridge is catalogued as kind 'other' (like CARD) because touch drives only its Tac-Retarget step; its GR00T N1.7 policy takes no touch input.

Judgment call: TARS (doi:10.1109/lra.2024.3505783, Tactile Affordance in Robot Synesthesia) was rejected because its abstract says tactile perception was simulated; the author-hosted PDF returned 404, so whether the four test tasks ran on a real tactile hand was not checked.
notes: 60 queue candidates (positions 0-59) decided, plus 3 more records: arxiv:2610.20320 (TacClaw-Infinity paper), the search hit Ti3D-contact and N0-Foundation / OpenNeoData from earlier notes. 63 in total; 4 models added, no datasets.

TacClaw-Infinity (arXiv 2610.20320, Daimon Robotics and 15 other institutions; 10,000+ h, 1M+ episodes announced, links 'Coming soon') was rejected as gripper only: a UMI-style handheld interface with fingertip tactile pads and gripper states.

N0-Foundation / OpenNeoData (arXiv 2608.29601, 5,000 h open subset on Hugging Face NeoteAIEmbodied/OpenNeoData) was rejected as gripper only; the paper says its representation targets parallel-jaw visuo-tactile fingers and leaves dexterous hands to future work.
VTG (doi:10.1109/lra.2024.3477168, three-finger grasp visual-tactile dataset, 18 objects per a TacCompress citation) set to 'later': closed access, and no hand model or download route was found.
HapticWAM (arXiv 2609.23888) and its three armteam Hugging Face sets are UR3 + Robotiq 2F-85 with Daimon DM-Tac W2L pads; rejected as gripper only.

Search hits already in the catalog or reviewed: TachinGlove (also the Tujian WRC 2026 expo page, which shows a 4,096-sensor e-skin hand and no dataset), TactiDex, VTouch++, SmartHand, ADL-21, UVTA, DexViTac, HORA, PalmDex, HapTile, RoboTacDex, Spark-0, TTP, TactAlign, UniTacHand, OSMO, DexTouch-WM, EgoPressure (models catalogued).
Still pending from earlier notes: DexMani arXiv 2608.00554 (abstract mentions no tactile sensing; full text not read) and the chang-xinhai and cyanhaze awesome-list items.
